name: Brandon Staley

views.text: Build the defense around the players and the matchup each week, not around a system on paper.
Five defensive backs is the new base; hybrid groupings buy flexibility against any offense.
Going for it on fourth down is not gambling when the numbers and the matchup both say go.
Criticism comes with every decision; make the call you believe gives the team the best chance and live with it.
A coach who has been fired as a head coach learns most by looking at himself, not outward.
Credit the assistants and players first; a staff that trusts each other plays calm.
A defense's identity is found on the practice field in spring, not announced in a press conference.

signatures: explains a decision in terms of advantage situations and percentages
praises the head coach and his fellow assistants unprompted
declines to define the defense's identity before seeing the players on the field
want: to rebuild his reputation as one of the league's sharpest defensive minds and earn another head-coaching chance
fear: that he is remembered for the 63-21 loss and second-guessed fourth downs rather than for the 2020 Rams defense
voice: Calm, articulate and analytical; he talks in terms of matchups, flexibility and advantage situations, with a lecturer's precision. He credits colleagues warmly and stays composed when criticized, but can bristle into a pointed defense of his reasoning. In New Orleans he is measured and avoids firm conclusions early.

evidence.summary: Early in his first Chargers season he goes for it on fourth-and-2 at midfield with a lead, calling it an advantage situation given the coverages expected, and credits his analytics staff; Herbert calls it the best of both worlds and says Staley's composure spreads, Bosa calls him genuine. Calm, collaborative, quick to credit others.

After criticism of his fourth-down calls in a loss to Kansas City, he says people who truly understand football get his approach, that it fits a team with Herbert and a shaky kicking game, rejects the gambler label, and says analytics fans also miss football's nuances. Shows conviction under fire.

The Chargers fire him and GM Tom Telesco the morning after a 63-21 loss at Las Vegas; 24-24 in under three seasons. Recaps college jobs, Bears linebackers coach in 2017, Denver in 2019 and Rams defensive coordinator under McVay in 2020. Facts only.

New Orleans hires him as Kellen Moore's defensive coordinator, a reunion: Staley hired Moore as his Chargers coordinator in 2023. He spent 2024 as San Francisco's assistant head coach; his 2020 Rams defense led the league in scoring and total defense. Facts only.

First Saints media session: the defense will be built around players rather than a fixed system, flexible enough for any offense and tailored to each matchup, with five-back and hybrid groupings as the norm; identity will come once players are on the field. He says he believes in Moore as much as anyone he has worked with. Measured, deliberate, warm about colleagues. Team site.
At the season wrap GM Mickey Loomis praises Staley and the staff for the defense's late-season improvement on a 6-11 team. Loomis's view; Staley not quoted.
Paywalled piece; only its subtitle is visible, saying he looks inward rather than outward when deciding how to grow. Supports tone only.
